name: aswath-thinking
title: aswath-thinking: Cognitive Reasoning & Inversion Architecture
tagline: Deconstruct ungrounded assumptions via first principles, inversion, and adversarial verification before executing code.
trigger: Use when approaching non-trivial architecture problems, ungrounded prompts, or complex decision trade-offs before any code is written.

modelCard.runtime: Cross-agent (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Cursor)

problem: AI coding assistants accept vague, high-level requests and immediately fabricate implementation code based on silent, ungrounded assumptions, leading to massive rewrites.
solution: Applies a 4-stage deconstruction protocol: 1) Identify every unproven assumption, 2) Invert the problem (how to make this system fail), 3) MECE decision branching, and 4) Concrete verification gate.

evaluation.proofText: Four stages: identify every unproven assumption, invert the problem, branch on the decision, then verify. The gate stops before any file is written.

comparisonTable.traditional: The agent guesses the requirement and writes it
comparisonTable.proposed: The assumption is named and inverted first

3. Core Choice: Local in-memory cache vs disk cache (User owns choice)
4. Decision: In-memory LRU chosen -> Proceed to spec.

name: aswath-first-principles
title: aswath-first-principles: Strict 10-Point Spec Gate
eyebrow: DECIDE BEFORE YOU BUILD · ZERO UNAPPROVED CODE
tagline: Strict pre-implementation gate: no code is written until an approved 10-section spec is reviewed by the user.
trigger: Use when a new project, feature, or build task has no approved spec yet, and work would otherwise start from assumptions.

modelCard.testCoverage: Enforced across all personal open-source projects

problem: Deciding during or after coding leads to unmaintainable systems. A retroactive spec only documents whatever happened to be built, not what was actually intended.
solution: Enforces an unskippable 8-step lifecycle: 1. Context, 2. Research, 3. Question Loop (max 4 multiple-choice questions with recommendations), 4. Spec drafting, 5. Self-review (zero TBDs), 6. Explicit user approval gate, 7. Mint skill, 8. Execute.

evaluation.proofText: Eight steps from context to execution, and seven of them end in a gate. Approval is a hard gate: nothing is scaffolded, no manifest is written, no stub lands, until the spec is approved.

comparisonTable.traditional: A summary of what you asked for
comparisonTable.proposed: A written spec you read and approve

name: aswath-chronicle
title: aswath-chronicle: Persistent Audit Trail & Git Ledger
tagline: Enforces recording decision milestones, user prompts, and rationale to disk with zero context inflation.
trigger: Use when building features, refactoring, or making non-trivial decisions that require a persistent audit trail of prompts, agent choices, and git history without wasting tokens.

modelCard.runtime: Cross-agent (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Cursor)
modelCard.transport: Local Disk Markdown Files & Git Tree

problem: AI agents frequently forget previous architectural decisions when conversation context is truncated or compacted. Re-explaining previous constraints wastes thousands of tokens, while non-documented decisions result in blind regressions.
solution: aswath-chronicle enforces a durable on-disk record: every user request, alternative considered, failure mode encountered, and technical decision is written directly to docs/interactions/session-ledger.md and committed atomically to git.

evaluation.proofText: Decisions and session records go to files under docs/ and never come back into the model context. The skill's own guidance puts the saving at 95%+, because a long architectural thread is read once and referenced by path after that.

comparisonTable.proposed: In files, next to the code

name: aswath-token-guard
title: aswath-token-guard: Context Window Discipline & Ledger
eyebrow: READ-ONCE DISCIPLINE · RTK FOLDING · CONTEXT LEDGER
tagline: Hooks enforcing read-once file discipline, command folding via rtk, and quiet context tracking.
trigger: Use when long-running sessions risk context bloat or when commands return verbose noisy output.

modelCard.contextTax: Reduces total token spend by 40-75% per session

problem: Uncontrolled agent runs fill context windows with repeated file reads, long raw git status outputs, and unfiltered test outputs. This leads to early degradation, lost context, and exorbitant token bills.
solution: aswath-token-guard enforces strict read-once discipline: it blocks re-reading already-read file regions, folds verbose command outputs via rtk, keeps a quiet ledger of actual tokens spent, and prompts deliberate compaction when the session ledger crosses 200k tokens.

evaluation.proofText: Token counts come from the usage objects the runtime reports, not from an estimate: Claude Code records them per assistant message, the MiniMax Code runtime per turn in its local database. The tool result share of the context runs around 90% on a busy session, and the biggest sessions here carry 200M+ tokens over a thousand turns - almost all of it context re-served rather than new. The tool names the files a session read more than once.

comparisonTable.proposed: Read once, cite the line range

name: aswath-compact
title: aswath-compact: Deliberate Context Compaction & Window Distillation
tagline: Distills long-running agent trajectories to high-signal milestones and releases the window when ledger exceeds 200k tokens.
installCommand: npx skills add aswathas/aswath-skills@aswath-minimax-compaction-handoff -g && npx skills add aswathas/aswath-skills@aswath-compact -g
trigger: Use when the session context ledger passes 200k tokens or when model instruction-following begins to drift.

modelCard.contextTax: Frees up 60-80% of current context window

problem: When conversation histories grow beyond 150k-200k tokens, LLM attention mechanisms degrade ('lost in the middle' effect). Automatic provider truncations drop critical architectural instructions arbitrarily.
solution: Performs deliberate, lossless distillation: extracts user constraints, verified facts, completed decisions, and active task state, discarding conversational chatter and verbose tool executions to restore full context headroom.

evaluation.proofText: The handoff carries Session Intent, Files Modified, Decisions Made, Current State and Next Steps - five sections, written to a file so the next session reads a page instead of replaying the window. The script extracts every fact verbatim from the session transcript: no model call, nothing guessed.

name: aswath-forge
title: aswath-forge: Capability Router & Catalog Verifier
tagline: Verification gateway ensuring minted skills and approved specs are checked before code is written.
trigger: Use at the start of any new project, feature, or build task to check for existing skills or when work would otherwise start from ungrounded assumptions.
problem: AI agents frequently rush to write code immediately upon receiving a prompt, hallucinating schemas and reinventing tools that already exist in the user's skill catalog.
solution: aswath-forge introduces a strict pre-execution gateway: it halts execution until it inspects local skill repositories (~/.gemini/skills, ~/.claude/skills) and checks whether a formal spec exists.

evaluation.proofText: Four steps: classify the task, look it up in the catalog, reuse or discover, then mint the skill if there is no match. Every finished task leaves a reusable skill behind, registered in the catalog with its provenance.

modelCard.testCoverage: Production rule across all personal agent environments

problem: Frontier models emit hundreds of tokens of polite greetings, restatements of the question, and speculative advice that the user never asked for, wasting tokens and user reading time.
solution: Enforces concise, caveman-style compression with everyday wording: short sentences, plain words, zero ceremonial pleasantries, and active pushback advocating for the smallest thing that actually works.
